notes: The ATW-3110 is a 2nd-generation 3000 Series UHF UniPak wireless system comprising the ATW-R310 true-diversity receiver and the ATW-T310 bodypack transmitter (paired with a lavalier/headworn mic, sold as e.g. ATW-3110b, depending on suffix/region). Ports listed are the receiver's rear panel and the transmitter's single I/O jack. Receiver: balanced XLRM output and unbalanced 1/4" (6.35mm) TS phone output are simultaneous, not switchable. Two BNC antenna inputs support true-diversity reception and can pass 12VDC bias for an optional active antenna/booster (e.g. ATW-B80) - modeled here as antenna signal inputs, not graded (no SDI/video bandwidth applies). DC power input is an external AC-to-12VDC adapter (barrel-style DC jack); exact barrel diameter not published. Transmitter input is a proprietary locking 4-pin connector (pin1 GND, pin2 INST, pin3 MIC, pin4 +5V DC bias) - not a standard XLR3/TRS; mapped to xlr4-dc as the closest listed 4-pin locking+DC-bias connector type, but the physical shell is a smaller locking connector (not full-size XLR), so treat with caution. No rack-mount ears are permanently attached; a rack-mount kit for pairing two half-rack units into 1U is an included/optional accessory, so rackUnits is omitted since the receiver ships as a half-rack desktop-style unit. Frequency band/channel specifics vary by region suffix and were not needed for I/O. Grades omitted throughout since none of the ports (XLR, TS, BNC antenna, DC power, locking 4-pin) fall on a gradeable connector scale.

ports.name: Input (Mic/Instrument)
ports.note: Proprietary locking 4-pin transmitter input jack (pin1 GND, pin2 INST, pin3 MIC, pin4 +5V DC bias); closest standard connector mapping, not a full-size XLR shell.
